quranic_mention: Named 43 times; one surah bears his name (Surah Nuh, 71)
teaser: Nine hundred and fifty years of calling. A handful believed. His own son drowned. And Allah still calls his mission a success — which should change what you think success means.

layers.title: Who
layers.subtitle: The first messenger sent to mankind, born into the first generation that ever worshipped an idol.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 4712 — the hadith of intercession, Anas ibn Malik
layers.content:
Ibn Kathir records that ten generations separated Adam from Nuh, and that in all of them people held to tawhid. Nuh was sent when that broke.

His people named their idols: «وَقَالُوا لَا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَيَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا» — "Do not abandon your gods: not Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr." (Quran 71:23) Ibn Abbas explained that these were the names of righteous men among the people of Nuh; when they died, their people erected images to honour them, and generations later those images were worshipped (recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, tafsir of Surah Nuh). Shirk did not arrive as rebellion. It arrived as excessive love for the righteous.

On the Day of Resurrection, when people seek someone to intercede, they will come to Nuh and say: "O Nuh, you are the first of the messengers Allah sent to the people of the earth." (Sahih al-Bukhari 4712) He is also one of the five given the title Ulul-'Azm — those of firm resolve (Quran 33:7, 42:13).

layers.title: The Call
layers.subtitle: Night and day, in public and in private, for nine and a half centuries.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
His own report of his method is preserved in the Quran: «رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا» — "My Lord, I called my people night and day." (Quran 71:5) Then: «ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًا • ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًا» — "Then I called them publicly. Then I appealed to them openly and confided to them privately." (Quran 71:8-9) Every channel. Every hour.

His message never changed: «يَا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُ» — "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him." (Quran 7:59)

And he made it attractive as well as urgent: seek forgiveness, and He will send rain, give you wealth and children, and make gardens for you (Quran 71:10-12).

Allah states the duration plainly: «فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا» — "he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty." (Quran 29:14) Nine hundred and fifty years of da'wah. Most of us give up on a relative after nine hundred and fifty days.

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: They mocked him while he built. His wife disbelieved. His son refused the ark and drowned.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
The mockery was constant: «وَيَصْنَعُ الْفُلْكَ وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُ» — "And he was constructing the ship, and whenever a company of the eminent of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him." (Quran 11:38) A ship, on dry land, with no sea in sight.

The result of nine and a half centuries: «وَمَا آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ» — "But none had believed with him except a few." (Quran 11:40)

The hardest loss was inside his own home. Allah names Nuh's wife among the disbelieving wives as a warning (Quran 66:10). And as the water rose, Nuh called out to his son: «يَا بُنَيَّ ارْكَب مَّعَنَا وَلَا تَكُن مَّعَ الْكَافِرِينَ» — "O my son, come aboard with us and be not with the disbelievers." The son answered: "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." Nuh said: "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah." And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned (Quran 11:42-43).

When Nuh pleaded for him, Allah answered: "He is not of your family; indeed, his deed was not righteous" (Quran 11:46). Ibn Kathir notes the lesson every believing parent must swallow: guidance is not inherited, and even a prophet cannot force it into a heart.

layers.title: The Miracle
layers.subtitle: A ship built by revelation, and a sign that began in an oven.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Allah commanded: «وَاصْنَعِ الْفُلْكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا» — "And construct the ship under Our observation and Our revelation." (Quran 11:37) The first great vessel in human history was built to a divine specification, in full view of people who laughed at every plank.

The signal to board was strange and exact: «حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ» — "until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed…" (Quran 11:40) Water gushing from a baking oven — the ordinary place of fire became the announcement of the flood. He was ordered to carry a pair of every kind, and his family except those already decreed to drown.

Then: «فَفَتَحْنَا أَبْوَابَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَاءٍ مُّنْهَمِرٍ • وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُونًا» — "Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down, and caused the earth to burst with springs." (Quran 54:11-12) Water from above and below at once. «وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ فِي مَوْجٍ كَالْجِبَالِ» — "and it sailed with them through waves like mountains." (Quran 11:42)

And he was taught what to say on boarding: «بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا» (Quran 11:41), and «الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي نَجَّانَا مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ» (Quran 23:28). Even in rescue, the tongue is trained toward Allah.

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: Almost no converts, and Allah calls it success. That should rearrange how you measure your own work.
layers.source: Ibn Kathir, Stories of the Prophets
layers.content:
Allah's verdict on Nuh is not measured in numbers: «وَلَقَدْ نَادَانَا نُوحٌ فَلَنِعْمَ الْمُجِيبُونَ • وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ • وَجَعَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُ هُمُ الْبَاقِينَ • وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ • سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ • إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ» — "And Nuh had certainly called Us, and We are the best of responders… and We made his descendants those who remained. And We left for him [favourable mention] among later generations: 'Peace upon Nuh among the worlds.' Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good." (Quran 37:75-80)

Every human alive descends from those who boarded. He is named among the Ulul-'Azm, the five of firm resolve, in Quran 33:7 and 42:13. On the Day of Judgment he is the first messenger people turn to (Sahih al-Bukhari 4712).

Ibn Kathir draws the conclusion the Quran forces: Nuh was not judged by conversion rates. He was judged by faithfulness to the command. «إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ» — this is how We reward those who do good.

So if you are trying to hold a family together, or call someone back, or simply stay upright in a bad environment and seeing nothing change: the standard you will be measured against is Nuh's standard, and it was never the size of the response. It was whether you kept calling.

quiz.prompt: How long does the Quran say Nuh remained among his people calling them?

options.text: Forty years
A thousand years minus fifty — 950 years
Three hundred and nine years
The Quran does not specify

quiz.citation: Quran 29:14 — «فَلَبِثَ فِيهِمْ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ إِلَّا خَمْسِينَ عَامًا»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Kathir notes this is the explicit text of the Quran, not an estimate — the longest recorded da'wah in human history, with the smallest recorded response.

quiz.prompt: According to Ibn Abbas, how did the idols Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq and Nasr come to be worshipped?

options.text: They were foreign gods brought by traders
They were carved by a king who demanded worship
They were righteous men whose images were made after their deaths, and later generations worshipped them
They were stars the people mistook for deities

quiz.citation: Quran 71:23; Ibn Abbas's explanation recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari, tafsir of Surah Nuh
quiz.scholar_reflection: Shirk entered mankind through excessive veneration of the righteous, not through open rebellion. That is why Islam is so strict about how the pious are honoured.

quiz.prompt: What was the sign that the flood had begun and it was time to board?

options.text: A comet appeared over the valley
The oven overflowed with water
The animals gathered on their own
Three days of total darkness

quiz.citation: Quran 11:40 — «حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَاءَ أَمْرُنَا وَفَارَ التَّنُّورُ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The place of fire became the source of water. Allah's signs often arrive in the last form we would have chosen to watch.

quiz.prompt: What did Allah reply when Nuh appealed for his drowning son?

options.text: He was saved on a mountain
"He is not of your family; indeed, his deed was not righteous"
Allah did not answer
He was returned to the ark

quiz.citation: Quran 11:46 — «إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Kinship to a prophet saves no one. The bond that counted on that day was faith, not blood — and Ibn Kathir draws this out as a mercy for every parent who has done their duty and still watched a child choose otherwise.

quiz.prompt: In the hadith of intercession, how do people address Nuh on the Day of Resurrection?

options.text: "You are the father of mankind"
"You are the Friend of Allah"
"You are the first of the messengers Allah sent to the people of the earth"
"You are the one who spoke with Allah"

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari 4712 — narrated by Anas ibn Malik
quiz.scholar_reflection: The first title belongs to Adam as the father of mankind; the first messengership belongs to Nuh. The hadith preserves the sequence precisely.

quiz.prompt: Nuh called for 950 years and few believed. When your effort produces no visible result, what usually happens inside you?

options.text: I quietly stop, telling myself it was never going to work
I keep going but grow resentful of the people I am trying to help
I start measuring myself by the response instead of by the effort
I can sustain it if I remember the outcome was never mine to control

quiz.citation: Quran 11:40 and Quran 37:80 — «إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: Allah praised Nuh's faithfulness, not his conversion rate. Detaching your sense of worth from other people's response is not indifference — it is how long-term obedience becomes survivable.
quiz.slider_label: How much does your persistence depend on seeing results?

quiz.prompt: They mocked him while he built a ship on dry land. Where do you feel the pull of other people's ridicule most?

options.text: In how visibly I practise my religion in public
In family settings, where old versions of me are expected
At work, where my values look inefficient or naive
Online, where anything sincere invites contempt

quiz.citation: Quran 11:38 — «وَكُلَّمَا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِّن قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُ»
quiz.scholar_reflection: The ark looked absurd right up until the water came. Obedience often looks foolish exactly as long as the test lasts, and not one second longer.
quiz.slider_label: How much does fear of mockery shape what you do?

quiz.prompt: Nuh's wife and son rejected him while he was a prophet of Allah. How do you carry the disbelief or distance of someone you love?

options.text: I blame myself for not doing or saying enough
I push harder, and it damages the relationship
I have withdrawn, because it hurts too much to keep trying
I keep the door open, make du'a, and leave the outcome to Allah

quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Kathir treats this as one of the great consolations in the Quran: if a prophet's sincerity could not guarantee his own son's faith, then your loved one's choice is not the verdict on your effort.
quiz.slider_label: How at peace are you with what you cannot control in them?

quiz.prompt: Shirk began among Nuh's people through excessive love of righteous men. Which form of over-attachment is most alive in your own heart?

options.text: Attachment to a teacher or scholar, more than to what they teach
Attachment to a person whose approval I need more than Allah's
Attachment to a role or identity that has quietly become the point
Attachment to a means — money, health, a plan — as if it were the Provider

quiz.citation: Quran 71:23; Ibn Abbas's explanation in Sahih al-Bukhari
quiz.scholar_reflection: The first idols were monuments to good people. Love that displaces Allah does not announce itself as shirk; it arrives dressed as loyalty.
quiz.slider_label: How central is Allah compared to that attachment?

quiz.prompt: Nuh was taught to say on boarding: "In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage." What is your instinct at the moment a plan finally moves?

options.text: Relief, and I forget to name Allah at all
Anxiety about what could still go wrong
Quiet credit-taking — I got us here
I turn to Allah first, in words, before anything else

quiz.scholar_reflection: The rescue was already decreed, and still he was taught the words. Naming Allah at the start of every departure is what keeps success from turning into self-congratulation.
quiz.slider_label: How habitual is turning to Allah when things start going well?
